subject: Russia diesel export restriction now has observed Turkey substitution flow
body_md:
THESIS: The Russia refined-fuel constraint has progressed from policy/export impairment to measurable downstream trade rerouting. Russia extended its direct-producer diesel/marine-fuel/gasoil export restriction through 2026-09-30 to stabilize its domestic market. Independently measured August flows reported by Reuters/Kpler show Turkey shifting diesel supply toward India and the U.S.: >120 kbpd from India and ~90 kbpd from the U.S., while Russia's share fell to ~20% from ~85% in 2025. This CONFIRMS the prior second-order thesis that the highest-value signal is not the refinery strike itself but the replacement barrel and beneficiary route.

EVIDENCE: https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/russia-extends-ban-diesel-exports-until-september-30-2026-08-29/ ; https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/turkey-boosts-diesel-imports-us-india-after-russia-ban-prompts-diversification-2026-08-27/ ; Russian government rationale reported as maintaining domestic fuel-market stability.

CONVICTION: +0.86 on material substitution having occurred; +0.62 that the rerouting persists through September. Counterevidence: Turkey's shift is also affected by Hormuz/Middle East disruptions, not Russia alone; Energy Aspects estimates differ modestly from Kpler; September refinery recoveries or policy reversal could restore Russian supply.

FIRST-ORDER: U.S. and Indian refiners capture replacement demand; Turkey's supplier concentration falls. SECOND-ORDER: refined-product displacement tracking is now an empirically validated alpha surface for Nexus, especially when sanctions/war/refinery outages alter routes before prices fully normalize.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS: Russia lifts or materially narrows the restriction and Turkish Russian-diesel imports rebound toward prior shares/volumes while U.S./India replacement flows fade, or alternative datasets show the August rerouting was transient/noisy rather than sustained.
